chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj and Hafsh ibn al-Bakhtari and Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said: We heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
Regarding a man who has a female slave, is she permissible for his son? He said: 'As long as it is not sexual intercourse or direct contact like intercourse, there is no harm.'

And it is not permissible for a man to marry the woman his son has contracted marriage with, in all cases. Allah the Exalted said: 'And the wives of your sons who are from your own loins,' so He prohibited by the apparent meaning of the word the wives of the children in general.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a man to marry the woman his son is married to in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between *jamāʿ* (full sexual intercourse) and *mubāsharah* (other forms of intimacy) regarding a father's rights over his son's female slave, permitting the latter while prohibiting the former. It further establishes the principle of *ʿaqd* (contract) over *ʿurf* (custom) in marital prohibitions, noting that while the Quran explicitly forbids marrying the wives of one's sons, the specific case of a slave girl married to a son is governed by the nature of the sexual act rather than the marital bond itself. This reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on precise textual interpretation (*zāhir al-lafẓ*) versus contextual application.
